findings.summary: Observed-return recurrence appends G_t then propagates with rewards[t] instead of rewards[t] before append; distance>=1 returns use the wrong reward index.
findings.failure_scenario: T=3 one slot, death at t=2, rewards a,b,c: start 1 yields c+gamma*c instead of b+gamma*c; start 0 yields b+gamma*c+gamma^2*c instead of a+gamma*b+gamma^2*c. observed_discounted_return_mean and time_to_death_bucket_means 1_4/5_16/17_plus are wrong; bucket counts still pass.
findings.consequence: Reported observed-death descriptive values are silently wrong; no control asserts observed-return values.
findings.fix: Compute ret = rewards[t] + GAMMA*ret_next at non-terminal steps before appending; add hand-value tests for observed returns and bucket means.

findings.summary: Partial raw variant is accepted with complete scaled components; the component path silently ignores the partial raw fields.
findings.failure_scenario: NPZ with score_reward, survival_reward, death_reward and only elapsed_raw_frames: load_npz passes (components <= keys), analyze takes component path (have_raw False, have_comp True).
findings.consequence: Raw accounting checks (elapsed bounds, alive == elapsed - terminated, score >= 0) are skipped, violating the exactly-one-variant contract. Untested.
findings.fix: Reject any partial raw set or partial component set in load_npz and analyze.

findings.summary: Parity compares only mean/variance to production; near-constant case asserts only target_variance > 0, not finite EV; no component-variant rejection tests.
findings.failure_scenario: Compensating element errors in target/advantage pass mean/variance parity; near-constant EV regressions to None or NaN are not caught.
findings.consequence: Test strength overstated relative to the claimed parity and no-epsilon EV checks.
findings.fix: Compare per-element target and advantage; assert finite EV for near-constant targets; add scaled-component rejection cases.

closed_from_r1: analyzer-vs-production moment parity for both lambdas plus hand terminal/reset/tail and truncation cases
